text:
Samira Khan: Hi team — planning to take intermittent parental leave (doctor expects a 2-week hospital stay plus intermittent follow-ups over 3 months). Im in CA so curious how SDI/PFL interact with Redwood top-up, and whether intermittent days count toward the 30-day benefits enrollment window. Also need a one-paragraph handoff my manager can post and a checklist for e-signing.

Luis (People Ops): Congrats Samira! Short answers first: CA State Disability Insurance (SDI) and Paid Family Leave (PFL) can cover wage replacement for qualifying periods; Redwood top-up layers on top per policy. Intermittent leave is allowed — submit each block of leave and we'll coordinate SDI/PFL claims. Benefits enrollment: you still have 30 days from the qualifying event (birth/placement) to add dependents. If intermittent starts before you file, we can initiate enrollment and amend dates later.

Nicole (Benefits): Add: for SDI/PFL you must file claims to EDD — we help with paperwork and can upload medical certs. Top-up: Redwood pays configured top-up for each paid leave day; payroll calculates it per-pay-period. If SDI benefit arrives after payroll, payroll will do a retro adjustment.

Samira Khan: Helpful. How should I record intermittent days so payroll matches SDI weeks? Any preferred format?

Luis (People Ops): Track intermittent days in the leave portal (link in the checklist). For payroll alignment, add each absence block with start/end dates and attach doctor notes if required. If you expect partial days, note hours (e.g., 4h clinic).

payroll-bot: Payroll note: To ensure correct top-up, submit leave entries at least 3 business days before payroll cutoff. Retro adjustments will be applied if claims come in after payroll. Include employee ID in submissions.

Nicole (Benefits): Also: enroll the newborn within 30 days for immediate coverage; if you miss the window, file an appeal and we'll route to benefits exceptions. For SDI/PFL timelines: file claims within 49 days of disability/leave start for best outcomes.

Samira Khan: Can I e-sign everything now and amend dates later if intermittent schedule changes?

Luis (People Ops): Yes — DocuSign supports anticipated dates. E-sign now, update entries in the portal later. We'll flag the file as "intermittent" so People Ops reviews changes weekly.

Luis (People Ops): Handoff paragraph you can copy/paste: 
``
Hi @team,
I'll be on intermittent parental leave starting START_DATE with expected hospital stay and follow-ups through END_DATE. Primary contact: MANAGER (email). Coverage: COVER_LEAD and CONTRACTOR will handle day-to-day; see runbooks: <link>. I'll do an overlap week on RETURN_OVERLAP for knowledge transfer. For urgent infra, use on-call.
Thanks, Samira
``

Samira Khan: Perfect — thanks. One last Q: does intermittent leave affect eligibility for the childcare stipend for the weeks Im partially working?

Nicole (Benefits): Childcare stipend is prorated by weeks on approved leave; partial-day clinic visits don't usually change stipend unless you take a full leave week. We'll calculate prorate and include breakdown in payroll estimate.

people-ops-bot: HR ticket opened: HR-PL-2026-811. People Ops will follow up with SDI/PFL claim checklist and DocuSign packet within 1 business day.

Samira Khan: Thank you all — uploading docs now and will log intermittent blocks as they happen. Appreciate the quick turnaround :heart:
